title: Cardinal Billing Account Rules Manual: Notice of Cancellation for Nonpayment, Rescission and Cancellation
content:
## Section 4. Nonpayment on the Cardinal Billing Account

4.1 **When a notice is mailed.** A notice of cancellation for nonpayment is mailed when an installment remains unpaid the pay plan's notice trigger days (calendar days) after its due date and the past-due amount is at least the pay plan's smallest past-due amount noticed. The past-due amount is, as of the evaluation date, the installment premium and fees whose due date has passed, less payments and credits posted, on the account. An unpaid amount within the pay plan's underpayment tolerance never triggers a notice. The notice trigger days are the figure of the account's own pay plan, for each of the six pay plans.

4.2 **Account status.** A notice is mailed only while the account status is current. The status is read from the company's record of that billing account before the notice is mailed.

4.3 **Cancellation effective date.** The cancellation effective date printed on the notice is the mail date plus the state notice days for the policy's governing state plus the pay plan's mailing allowance days, at the pay plan's cancellation effective time.

4.4 **Amount required to rescind.** The amount required to rescind is the full past-due amount on the mail date, including fees; amounts falling due after the mail date are not part of it.

4.5 **Rescission.** The notice is rescinded only when the amount required to rescind is received no later than the pay plan's rescission cutoff days (calendar days) after the cancellation effective date printed on the notice. Payments are counted by posting date, the cancellation effective date being day 0, so a payment posted on the cancellation effective date itself rescinds the notice. The cancellation effective date is read from that notice's entry on the account's billing history.

4.6 **Partial payment.** A partial payment does not rescind and leaves the cancellation effective date unchanged.

4.7 **Cancellation.** When the cancellation effective date passes without the cure, the policy is cancelled for nonpayment. Earned premium is computed pro rata to the cancellation effective date and the return premium is credited to the account, and a final bill for any remaining earned balance is issued, due in the pay plan's earned-premium due days.

## Worked dates (hypothetical)

A notice on a Virginia policy is mailed on day M. The state notice days are 15 and the mailing allowance 5, so the cancellation effective date is day M plus 20, at the plan's effective time.

| Posting date of the full amount required to rescind | Rescission cutoff 0 days | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Day M plus 19 | Before the cancellation effective date | Notice rescinded |
| Day M plus 20 | On the cancellation effective date (day 0) | Notice rescinded |
| Day M plus 21 | One day after | Not rescinded; the policy is cancelled for nonpayment |

A payment of part of the amount required to rescind, posted on day M plus 10, does not rescind, and the cancellation effective date stays day M plus 20.

## Amount required to rescind (hypothetical)

On the mail date the account shows an unpaid installment of $110.00 and a late fee of $15.00, both past due, and a further installment falls due five days after the mail date. The amount required to rescind is $125.00; the later installment is not part of it.
